memories.author: D03
memories.text: Fatigue and mild right upper quadrant discomfort. PRESENTING COMPLAINT: 64‑year‑old male driver reports intermittent fatigue and a dull ache in the right hypochondrium for 2 weeks, worse after heavy meals. No jaundice, pruritus or weight loss. EXAMINATION: BP 128/82 mmHg, weight 78 kg, height 1.68 m, BMI 27.6 (obese). Abdomen soft, mild tenderness in right hypochondrium, no hepatomegaly or ascites. IMPRESSION: Probable non‑alcoholic fatty liver disease, obesity‑related. Start silymarin 140 mg TDS and rosuvastatin 5 mg OD. Order fasting lipid profile, fasting blood sugar, liver function tests, platelet count and abdominal ultrasound. ARRANGEMENTS: Review in 6 weeks with labs. Advise reduced saturated fat, increase vegetables, walk 30 min daily. Return if: chest pain, breathlessness, fever >39°C, vomiting, blood in stools, worsening abdominal pain.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Abdominal ultrasound: Liver size 15 cm in mid‑clavicular line. Diffuse increased hepatic echogenicity consistent with steatosis. No focal lesion, no biliary dilatation. Spleen normal. No ascites. Platelet count not imaged.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Liver function: ALT 48 U/L (ref 7‑35), AST 28 U/L (ref 8‑33). Alkaline phosphatase 78 U/L (ref 40‑129). GGT 32 U/L (ref 9‑48). Bilirubin total 0.9 mg/dL (ref 0.2‑1.2). Fasting lipid: Cholesterol 202 mg/dL (<200), Triglycerides 158 mg/dL (<150), HDL 38 mg/dL (>40), LDL 124 mg/dL (<100). Platelet count 225 x10^9/L (150‑400).

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Via clinic app: Still feeling tired after long drives. The right side ache comes after eating fried food, lasts about an hour, then goes away. No nausea. Taking silymarin three times daily and rosuvastatin at night as prescribed.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Follow‑up on NAFLD and lifestyle. PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Persistent mild fatigue, right‑sided discomfort after heavy meals reduced in frequency. EXAMINATION: BP 130/84 mmHg, weight 77 kg, BMI 27.2 (obese). Abdomen soft, no tenderness. IMPRESSION: NAFLD, obesity, mild ALT elevation. Continue silymarin 140 mg TDS, rosuvastatin 5 mg OD. Advise strict low‑fat diet, avoid sugary drinks, increase activity to 45 min brisk walk most days. Order repeat LFT in 8 weeks. ARRANGEMENTS: Review in 2 months. Return if: worsening pain, jaundice, dark urine, fever >39°C, unexplained weight loss.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Liver function: ALT 32 U/L (ref 7‑35), AST 24 U/L (ref 8‑33). Alkaline phosphatase 76 U/L, GGT 30 U/L. Bilirubin normal. Platelet count 228 x10^9/L.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Referral to Dr S. Rao, Gastroenterology, Vikram Hospital, for further evaluation of NAFLD and cardiovascular risk. Reason: Persistent mild liver enzyme elevation despite lifestyle, need fibrosis assessment. Attach recent LFT, lipid profile, ultrasound report. Request FibroScan and hepatology opinion.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Post‑referral update. PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports gastroenterology appointment scheduled for Jan 2026; still occasional fatigue, no new symptoms. EXAMINATION: BP 128/80 mmHg, weight 76.5 kg, BMI 27.1 (obese). Abdomen benign. IMPRESSION: NAFLD, obesity, awaiting gastroenterology input. Continue silymarin 140 mg TDS, rosuvastatin 5 mg OD. Order fasting lipid profile and fasting blood sugar (annual) and repeat LFT in 3 months. ARRANGEMENTS: Review after gastroenterology visit. Advise Mediterranean diet, limit alcohol to <20 g/day, walk 45 min daily. Return if: acute abdominal pain, vomiting, fever >39°C, jaundice, swelling of legs.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Letter from Dr S. Rao, Gastroenterology: FibroScan shows CAP 260 dB/m (consistent with steatosis), stiffness 6.2 kPa (F0‑F1). No significant fibrosis. Advise continue current regimen, repeat LFT and lipid profile in 3 months, reassess need for vitamin E. No further hepatology follow‑up required unless enzymes rise.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Fasting lipid: Cholesterol 190 mg/dL, Triglycerides 140 mg/dL, HDL 40 mg/dL, LDL 110 mg/dL. Fasting blood sugar 92 mg/dL (ref 70‑99). Liver function: ALT 28 U/L, AST 22 U/L, bilirubin normal. Platelet count 230 x10^9/L.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Review of labs and cardiovascular risk. PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient feels better, less fatigue, occasional mild right‑sided discomfort after heavy meals, now rare. EXAMINATION: BP 126/78 mmHg, weight 75 kg, BMI 26.6 (overweight). Abdomen soft. IMPRESSION: NAFLD, obesity, improved liver enzymes, LDL near target. Increase rosuvastatin to 10 mg OD to further lower LDL; continue silymarin 140 mg TDS. Advise maintain weight loss, aim BMI <25, continue Mediterranean diet, walk 50 min daily. Order repeat LFT and lipid profile in 4 months. ARRANGEMENTS: Review in 4 months. Return if: chest pain, breathlessness, fever >39°C, vomiting, blood in stools, worsening abdominal pain.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Liver function: ALT 22 U/L (ref 7‑35), AST 20 U/L (ref 8‑33), bilirubin normal. Alkaline phosphatase 74 U/L, GGT 28 U/L. Platelet count 232 x10^9/L.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Booking: Follow‑up visit with Dr Priya Natarajan (D03) scheduled for 2026-09-15 at 10:30 AM. Patient confirmed via phone.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Six‑month follow‑up. PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports good energy, no abdominal discomfort, occasional mild tiredness after long drives. EXAMINATION: BP 124/76 mmHg, weight 73.5 kg, BMI 26.0 (overweight). Abdomen benign. IMPRESSION: NAFLD, obesity, stable liver enzymes, LDL on target with rosuvastatin 10 mg OD. Continue silymarin 140 mg TDS, rosuvastatin 10 mg OD. Advise maintain weight, aim BMI <25, continue diet and activity. Order repeat LFT and lipid profile annually. ARRANGEMENTS: Review in 6 months or sooner if symptoms. Return if: chest pain, breathlessness, fever >39°C, vomiting, blood in stools, worsening abdominal pain.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Liver function: ALT 20 U/L (ref 7‑35), AST 18 U/L (ref 8‑33), bilirubin normal. Alkaline phosphatase 72 U/L, GGT 26 U/L. Fasting lipid: Cholesterol 185 mg/dL, Triglycerides 130 mg/dL, HDL 42 mg/dL, LDL 105 mg/dL. Platelet count 235 x10^9/L.
